problem:
The fourth-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by

$$
{P}_{4}(x)=1+3x+\frac{9}{2}{x}^{2}-\frac{9}{2}{x}^{3}+\frac{27}{8}{x}^{4}.
$$

What is ${f}^{‴}(0)?$

${f}^{‴}(0)=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
The coefficient of ${x}^{3}$ is given by $\frac{{f}^{‴}(0)}{3!}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{‴}(0)}{3!} & =-\frac{9}{2} \\ \frac{{f}^{‴}(0)}{6} & =-\frac{9}{2} \\ {f}^{‴}(0) & =-27.\end{aligned}
$$
